title: Safety-relevant disconnect device does not confirm its commanded state
engineering_question: A safety-relevant device failed to confirm its commanded state in the field. What is the containment position, the likely cause, and what corrective action is required?
one_liner: Identify the likely causes of this field failure and the required containment.
initial_input: A vehicle in fleet trial reported a fault indicating that a high voltage disconnect device did not confirm the open state after a DC fast charge session.
expected_reasoning_paths: Severity is at the top of the scale because the failure effect is HV present at the inlet, so containment precedes root cause
TR-058 passes but was performed on the main contactor, not the DC charge contactor pair, so it does not cover the failing part
TR-057 reproduces the failure on 1 of 6 units on the bench, so this is a population characteristic rather than a single field anomaly
SI-006 escalation to the supplier is justified by bench reproduction
known_unknowns: Total fleet exposure count is not represented in the environment
Contactor interruption history per vehicle is not available
No confirmed root cause exists - no RootCause record links to QI-013
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
